historical_reviews.history: Round-2 left this source row UNRESOLVED. No approved switch-board specification or case-specific ruling was found.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Wistron I2C defaults to BMC/platform-management scope; a host-visible scan is not proof that the switch-board sideband path was reached.

original_test_intent: Validate the switch board's management I2C path and expected attached devices according to its platform specification, distinct from motherboard, PSU and other board segments.
original_method: Because the only method and criterion point to an unavailable specification, no controller discovery, mux traversal, address probe or device read is authorized. The case requires a fresh review after the switch-board contract is supplied.
manual_activity: Switch/platform owners must identify the SW_BD hardware revision and publish its sideband controller, mux, device map, permitted reads and acceptance contract.
required_inputs: Owning BMC/OOB controller and access method
Expected switch, EEPROM and sensor identities/responses
safety_requirements: Do not equate all host I2C buses with SW_BD
Do not probe an unknown switch sideband branch
Do not access configuration or EEPROM command space
Do not use force or write-capable operations
Preserve switch/fabric, BMC and OS state evidence
Stop on link, management, sensor or bus anomaly
agent_execution_scope: Reject generic all-bus discovery as the test
Await approved spec and fresh review
engineer_actions: Define expected responses and fabric-health checks

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Scanning every host-visible adapter neither selects the SW_BD mux branch nor proves the expected switch devices. Generic address probes may reach live sideband, EEPROM or sensor endpoints, while head -20 discards part of the address map.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: BLOCKED: provide the exact switch-board management topology and approved transaction/oracle before constructing a bounded probe.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The I2C SW_BD identity and two-minute estimates are preserved; no controller, address or device response is invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Once defined, access SW_BD through the approved BMC/OOB controller, traverse only the documented mux branch, read only allowlisted identity/status fields and compare them to the board-revision matrix while monitoring switch/fabric and platform management health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces a placeholder and unsafe global scan with a board-revision-specific sideband verification.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Enumerating adapters cannot prove mux selection, switch-board identity, expected components or uninterrupted fabric state.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A sideband transaction can contend with switch management or touch configuration/EEPROM space; a recovery path must remain independent of the affected board.

project_override_considerations: Under the Wistron ownership rule, treat SW_BD I2C as BMC/platform scope unless its specification explicitly states otherwise; require BMC controller, mux branch, addresses and expected output.
expected_evidence: Approved SW_BD specification and fresh review
Board revision, BMC/controller and mux-path identity
Allowlisted addresses, device types and permitted register/transaction
Complete raw responses matched to the switch-board BOM
Pre/post switch links/fabric state plus BMC SEL/SDR/sensor and OS health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria do not contradict each other; Procedure and Criteria are unusable because the referenced switch-board specification is absent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The missing specification is required to distinguish the switch-board sideband segment from other I2C domains and to define a safe transaction and expected response. Those semantics cannot be supplied by an i2c-tools package or approval alone.

engineering_decision_request.question: Define Functionality row 1801 Wistron-HW-00003-V003 I2C SW_BD: exact switch-board/revision, BMC or OOB owner and access path, controller/mux/bus/address/device map, permitted identity/status reads, expected responses, switch/fabric health acceptance, stop conditions and independent recovery; preserve Master placeholders and require fresh review.

review_improvement: Makes the physical SW_BD sideband identity and fabric-impact boundary explicit and blocks the case until the referenced contract exists.
independent_technical_reasoning: A switch board often sits behind a dedicated mux branch and may expose management, EEPROM and sensor functions with different safety properties. The same numerical address on a different branch is a different device. Therefore a global scan cannot demonstrate SW_BD coverage, and without a board/revision response matrix there is no PASS oracle or safe target.
